AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The prognostic relevance of primary location of urothelial carcinoma (UC) on survival has been poorly investigated.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The prospectively collected data from three EORTC advanced UC studies 30924 (M-VAC versus high dose M-VAC), 30986 (MCAVI versus GC arm, among patients unfit for CDDP) and 30987 (GC-Paclitaxel versus GC, among patients fit for CDDP) were used. Patients were grouped by primary tumor location as bladder (BCa) versus upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). PFS and OS by tumor location were tested using Cox proportional hazard regression stratified by study and treatment using a 2-sided alpha of 0.05.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Of the 1,039 patients, 878 (85.3%) and 161 (14.7%) had BCa and UTUC, respectively. BCa patients had a better performance status and were more likely to be of male gender (p=0.008 und p=<0.074, respectively). With a median follow up of 4.8 years (IQR: 4.0-6.7), 733 patients died and 925 experienced disease progression. OS and PFS did not differ significantly between BCa and UTUC (p=0.3 and p=0.7, respectively), even after adjusting for the effects of Bajorin risk groups within each tumor location. When UTUC were considered separately, the effects of the patients with primary ureter tumors had a better OS (odds ratio[OR] =0.74, p=0.047) compared to patients with primary BCa. However, this association did not remain significant after adjustment for Bajorin risk groups (p=0.05).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The location of the primary tumor had no impact on PFS or OS in patients with locally advanced or metastatic UC treated with platinum-based combination chemotherapy.
